basis_for_inclusion: The ABCG2 Y581S missense mutation is the cause of the chromosome-6 (BTA6) QTL with a major effect on milk yield and composition (fat/protein) in Holstein cattle.

Aurora kinase A regulates polyadenylation/translation of maternal mRNAs, chromosome segregation and polar-body extrusion during bovine oocyte meiotic maturation, and is a key regulator of developmental competence for early embryo development in cattle.

BCL2L1 (Bcl-xL) is an anti-apoptotic gene explicitly upregulated in bovine granulosa cells under acute heat stress, acting in cell survival against oxidative-stress-mediated apoptosis in a context of declining steroidogenesis, supporting its role as a candidate in reproduction under heat stress in cattle.

BMP15 is an oocyte-specific factor (TGF-beta superfamily) secreted by the oocyte that organises granulosa/theca cells in the cumulus-oocyte complex and is a determinant of oocyte competence/quality and follicular development in cattle.

Executioner caspase upregulated in bovine granulosa cells under acute heat stress, mediating oxidative-stress-induced apoptosis with concomitant decline in steroidogenesis (P4/E2), directly linking CASP3 to reproduction under heat stress in cattle.

CYP11A1 (cytochrome P450 side-chain cleavage) is a key ovarian steroidogenesis gene. In bovine granulosa cells under heat stress it was assessed by RT-PCR among steroidogenic genes (StAR, CYP11A1, CYP19A1, SF-1) and its mRNA was reduced by heat, in parallel with granulosa-cell apoptosis via the BAX/BCL-2 pathway and reduced E2 synthesis, linking CYP11A1 to steroidogenesis, granulosa apoptosis and the heat-stress response in cattle.
reference: Li L, Wu J, Luo M, Sun Y, Wang G (2016)

basis_for_inclusion: The non-conservative K232A substitution in DGAT1 (BTA14) is the causal variant of a major-effect QTL for milk fat content/yield in dairy cattle, supporting its inclusion in a candidate-gene panel for milk production and milk fat.

DNAJB1 (DnaJ/HSP40 family member B1) is a heat-shock co-chaperone central to the cellular heat-shock response. In Caracu, a tropically adapted Bos taurus beef breed, blood-plasma LC-MS/MS proteomics comparing the 7 most vs 7 least thermotolerant bulls (selected from 61 via a heat tolerance index) identified DNAJB1 among the differentially abundant proteins and as a protein-protein-interaction network node, naming it explicitly as a potential biomarker for thermotolerance/heat tolerance in cattle. This provides a real, cattle-specific (Bos taurus) functional/expression-under-heat-stress justification for curating DNAJB1 into a heat-stress candidate panel.
reference: de Freitas AC, Reolon HG, Abduch NG, Baldi F, Silva RMO, Lourenco D, Fragomeni BO, Paz CCP, Stafuzza NB (2024)

basis_for_inclusion: According to PubMed, Saravanan et al. (2021, Genomics) performed genome-wide selection-signature scans (iHS, ROH, Fst) on 12 indicine and taurine cattle breeds using BovineSNP50 data and explicitly identified DNAJB4 — alongside other heat-shock/chaperone genes (HSPA1L, HSPA1B) — as a candidate gene linked to production traits and adaptation of indigenous cattle to local environmental constraints such as heat stress. This directly justifies DNAJB4's inclusion in a curated panel of thermotolerance/heat-shock candidates in cattle: it is a real cattle/Bos taurus selection-signature association with heat stress. (Corroborating: Lindholm-Perry et al. 2016, Front Genet, PMID 27504120, found DNAJB4 up-regulated within a stress-response/heat-shock gene cluster in beef cattle spleen transcriptome.)

DNLZ was identified as a key gene in the dairy-cow heat-stress response (Bos taurus). The WGBS study of Yang et al. (2025, BMC Genomics) showed that, between spring and summer cows, DNLZ CpG-island promoter methylation increases under heat stress and is negatively correlated with its expression (confirmed by dual-luciferase assay); protein-protein-interaction analysis indicated high DNLZ connectivity, proposing it as a target/epigenetic marker for selecting heat-tolerant cattle.
reference: Yang Y, Chen Y, Hu L, Zhang C, Chen G, Hou L, Xu Q, Wang Y, Li M (2025)

basis_for_inclusion: DNMT1 (DNA methyltransferase 1) maintains DNA methylation patterns, an epigenetic mechanism mediating the heat-stress response in cattle. Masroor et al. (2022) showed that acute heat shock in PBMCs of zebu (Bos indicus) and crossbred (Bos indicus x Bos taurus) cattle alters DNMT1 expression (with DNMT3a/TET) and that hypomethylation facilitates stress-gene expression (HSP70, STIP1), linking DNMT1 to thermotolerance and epigenetic regulation under heat stress in cattle.
reference: Masroor S, Aalam MT, Khan O, Tanuj GN, Gandham RK, Dhara SK, Gupta PK, Mishra BP, Dutt T, Singh G, Sajjanar BK (2022)

basis_for_inclusion: DNMT3A (DNA methyltransferase 3 alpha) is a de novo DNA methyltransferase directly relevant to the panel trait of reproduction/epigenetic regulation under heat stress in cattle. This reference experimentally measured DNMT3a expression alongside DNMT1 and TET demethylases in cultured PBMCs subjected to acute heat shock in zebu (Bos indicus) and crossbred (Bos indicus x Bos taurus) dairy cattle, linking DNA methylation machinery to thermotolerance and stress-gene regulation. It justifies inclusion as a curated candidate via the function + expression-under-heat-stress-in-cattle criterion (cattle/Bos taurus crossbred, on-trait for DNA methylation under thermal stress).
reference: Masroor S, Aalam MT, Khan O, Tanuj GN, Gandham RK, Dhara SK, Gupta PK, Mishra BP, Dutt T, Singh G, Sajjanar BK (2022)

basis_for_inclusion: DNMT3B (DNA methyltransferase 3 beta) is a de novo DNA methyltransferase central to establishing DNA methylation patterns, the molecular basis of the panel trait. The cited study (according to PubMed) measures DNMT3b among key methylation regulators in bovine (Bos taurus) granulosa cells, directly linking the gene to DNA methylation machinery and granulosa-cell reproductive function in cattle — supporting its inclusion as a curated candidate for reproduction/DNA-methylation phenotypes. The reference is bovine and granulosa-cell focused but is not specific to heat stress.
reference: Floccari S, Sabry R, Choux L, Neal MS, Khokhar JY, Favetta LA (2024)

basis_for_inclusion: FASN (fatty acid synthase) is the positional candidate gene underlying the BTA19 QTL affecting milk and adipose fatty-acid composition (e.g., myristic acid C14:0) in cattle; SNPs in bovine FASN are associated with de novo synthesized milk-fat fatty acids, making it a core milk-fat / milk-production candidate.

GDF9 is an oocyte-secreted factor (TGF-beta family) that organises granulosa/theca cells in the oocyte-cumulus-follicle complex and is a determinant of follicular competence and oocyte quality in cattle.

GH1 (growth hormone 1) is the pituitary effector of the somatotropic axis (GH1-GHR-IGF1), the central regulator of postnatal growth and weight gain in cattle. Dani et al. (2012) showed in 736 Nellore (Bos indicus) bulls that stepwise substitution of shorter by longer GH1 promoter alleles was significantly associated with increased body weight gain (W550, weight at 550 days) and average daily gain (ADG), with a best-fit model indicating a 3- to 6-fold larger effect of GH1 promoter variation on ADG than variation at GHR or the IGF1 microsatellite, plus a threshold effect on ADG. This direct association/QTL evidence for growth and weight gain in beef cattle justifies including GH1 in a curated candidate panel for the somatotropic/growth trait.

GHR (growth hormone receptor) harbours the F279Y transmembrane-domain polymorphism, mapped to the chromosome-20 (BTA20) QTL affecting milk yield and composition (fat and protein percentage) in dairy cattle.

GHSR (growth hormone secretagogue receptor / ghrelin receptor) sits in a BTA1 region previously associated with feed intake and weight gain in beef cattle. Lindholm-Perry et al. (2011, Animal Genetics) evaluated polymorphisms within GHSR (and SLC2A2) in this QTL region, providing a direct cattle-specific association/QTL rationale for including GHSR in a curated panel of growth/weight-gain candidates linked to the somatotropic (ghrelin-GH) axis.

According to PubMed, this 2025 BMC Genomics whole-genome bisulfite sequencing study of dairy cows (spring vs. summer) identified GNAS among the three most significantly changed genes whose promoter DNA methylation was negatively correlated with expression in the heat stress response. This directly supports including GNAS in a curated panel of cattle thermotolerance / heat-stress candidates: it is a bovine (Bos taurus, dairy cow) study showing differential methylation and expression of GNAS under heat stress. DOI: https://doi.org/10.1186/s12864-025-11683-x
reference: Yang Y, Chen Y, Hu L, Zhang C, Chen G, Hou L, Xu Q, Wang Y, Li M (2025)

basis_for_inclusion: HSF1 (heat shock factor 1) is the master transcription factor that activates heat shock protein expression during the heat stress response in cattle. Rong et al. (2019) genotyped a missense SNP (NC_037341.1 g.616087A>G, rs135258919; Val>Ala) in the bovine HSF1 gene across 941 animals from 35 Chinese cattle breeds and found its allele/genotype frequencies were significantly associated (P<0.01) with annual temperature, relative humidity and the temperature humidity index (THI), indicating association with heat tolerance in indicine cattle. This provides a direct genetic-association (candidate SNP) justification for including HSF1 in a curated panel of thermotolerance candidates, on the Bos taurus (NC_037341.1) reference.

HSP90AA1 encodes the stress-inducible HSP90 alpha chaperone, central to the cellular heat-shock response. In Holstein cattle, acute heat stress (42 C) upregulates HSP90AA1, and functional SNPs in the gene (notably rs109256957 in the 3' UTR, modulating bta-miR-1224 binding) are significantly associated with thermotolerance traits (rectal temperature, respiration score). This combines association/genetic-variant evidence, function, and heat-stress-induced expression directly in Bos taurus, justifying inclusion in a curated panel of thermotolerance candidate genes.
reference: Hu L, Fang H, Abbas Z, Luo H, Brito LF, Wang Y, Xu Q (2024)

basis_for_inclusion: Heat-shock protein 90-kDa beta gene whose polymorphisms (notably the intron SNP g.4338T>C) are directly associated with heat tolerance in cattle. Charoensook et al. (2011) sequenced bovine HSP90AB1 across Bos taurus (Holstein Friesian) and Bos indicus (Thai native White Lamphun, Mountain cattle) and linked the T allele to improved heat-tolerance coefficient and physiological thermoregulation traits (respiration rate, rectal temperature), proposing HSP90AB1 SNPs as genetic markers for selecting cattle adapted to hot climates. This provides a real association/QTL-type justification for including the gene in a curated thermotolerance candidate panel. The same SNP was later replicated in Indian dairy cattle (Sajjanar et al. 2015, PMID 25153455).

Astuti et al. (2022, Sci Rep) validated HSPA12A SNPs by KASP-PCR across 720 sheep from 17 breeds adapted to different climates and confirmed HSPA12A as a candidate marker for thermotolerance/heat-stress adaptation in ruminant livestock. This directly justifies its inclusion in a curated heat-stress/thermotolerance candidate panel. Note: the validation was in sheep (Ovis aries), not cattle. A genuinely bovine reference (Masoudi et al. 2008, Anim Genet, PMID 18254734, Bos taurus) also lists HSPA12A as a positional/functional candidate, but for a muscular anomaly trait rather than thermotolerance, so it does not support the heat-stress rationale.

HSPA12B (heat shock protein A12B) is directly supported as a thermal-adaptation candidate in cattle: this study identified HSPA12B under positive selection in cold-adapted Chinese cattle breeds via 777K SNP genotyping and functionally validated it (knockout mouse) as a negative regulator of adipose browning and thermogenesis. This connects HSPA12B to heat-shock protein function and thermal/temperature-stress homeostasis in Bos taurus, justifying its inclusion in a curated panel of thermotolerance/heat-stress candidates (selection signature + function in cattle).

HSPA1A (HSP70 family) is a core heat-shock protein whose expression is a validated biomarker of the heat-stress response in cattle. Elayadeth-Meethal et al. (2022, J Therm Biol) directly profiled HSPA1A gene expression across heat-tolerant tropically adapted dwarf breeds (Vechur, Kasaragod) versus crossbred cattle, showing significant differences in HSPA1A expression between lineages and across temperature-humidity index (THI) levels, and explicitly proposed HSPA1A as a marker for selecting heat-tolerant animals. This supports its inclusion in a curated panel of thermotolerance/heat-stress candidate genes for Bos taurus.
reference: Elayadeth-Meethal M, Keambou Tiambo C, Poonkuzhi Naseef P, Saheer Kuruniyan M, K Maloney S (2022)

basis_for_inclusion: HSPA1B encodes an inducible Hsp70 molecular chaperone central to the cellular heat-shock response. Nayak et al. (2024), via selection-signature analyses (Tajima's D, CLR, iHS, ROH) on Bovine 50K data from eight Indian cattle breeds adapted to diverse climates, identified HSPA1B among adaptation genes within positive-selection regions linked to high-temperature/thermotolerance adaptation. This provides a real, cattle-specific (Bos taurus/indicus) genomic justification for including HSPA1B in a curated thermotolerance/heat-stress candidate panel. Attribution: based on articles retrieved from PubMed.
reference: Nayak SS, Panigrahi M, Rajawat D, Ghildiyal K, Sharma A, Jain K, Bhushan B, Dutt T (2024)

basis_for_inclusion: HSPA1L (heat shock protein 70 family member) is a curated thermotolerance candidate in cattle: a deletion mutation in its promoter region amplifies the transcriptional heat-shock response and confers cellular protection / increased embryo survival under heat shock, directly linking HSPA1L genetic variation to heat-stress tolerance in Bos taurus. Ortega et al. (2016, J Dairy Sci) experimentally show the thermoprotective HSPA1L allele protects bovine zygotes from heat shock, justifying its inclusion in a heat-stress candidate panel.

HSPA2 is an inducible HSP70-family chaperone central to the bovine heat-stress response. This study measured HSPA2 mRNA expression in dermal fibroblasts of zebu (Tharparkar) vs crossbred (Karan-Fries) cattle exposed to 25-44 C, showing HSPA2 up-regulation under heat stress and breed-dependent differences in thermotolerance (higher inducible HSP70 induction in the less heat-adapted Karan-Fries). This provides direct experimental cattle (Bos taurus/indicus) evidence for HSPA2 function under thermal stress, justifying its inclusion in a curated thermotolerance candidate panel.
reference: Singh AK, Upadhyay RC, Malakar D, Kumar S, Singh SV (2014)

basis_for_inclusion: Direct cattle (Bos taurus, Chinese Holstein) association study that sequenced HSPA4 and identified five SNPs significantly associated with rectal temperature, a heat-stress trait, validating HSPA4 as a thermotolerance candidate gene for genetic selection without compromising milk production. Strongly justifies inclusion in a curated heat-stress candidate panel.
reference: Xu J, Hu L, Ning J, Zhang F, Xu Q, Wang Y (2025)

basis_for_inclusion: HSPA5 encodes GRP78/BiP, the master endoplasmic-reticulum chaperone and central sensor of the unfolded protein response. Yang et al. (2021) experimentally show that in bovine mammary epithelial cells (MAC-T) acute heat stress (42C) upregulates heat-shock chaperones and drives GRP78 (HSPA5) protein expression and PERK phosphorylation, with the PERK/GRP78 ER-stress axis mediating heat-induced oxidative injury and apoptosis. This provides direct cattle (Bos taurus) functional/expression evidence that HSPA5 is responsive to and mechanistically involved in the cellular heat-stress response, justifying its inclusion in a curated panel of thermotolerance/heat-shock candidate genes.
reference: Yang M, Kuang M, Wang G, Ali I, Tang Y, Yang C, Li Y, Li L (2021)

basis_for_inclusion: HSPA6 (Heat Shock Protein Family A Hsp70 Member 6) is an inducible chaperone central to the cellular heat-shock response. This study directly measured HSPA6 (and HSF1) mRNA expression alongside physiological thermotolerance indicators (respiratory rate, rectal temperature) in taurine cattle (Angus and Simmental) subjected to a heat-tolerance test, finding that less-adapted animals had higher HSPA6 expression. It concludes HSPA6 expression can serve as an indicator of thermotolerance in cattle, providing a direct cattle/Bos taurus expression-under-heat-stress rationale for inclusion in a curated thermotolerance candidate panel.
reference: de Fátima Bretanha Rocha R, Baena MM, de Cássia Estopa A, Gervásio IC, Guaratini Ibelli AM, Santos Gionbelli TR, Gionbelli MP, Fonseca de Freitas RT, Conceição Meirelles SL (2019)

basis_for_inclusion: HSPA8 is a member of the HSP70 molecular chaperone family central to the cellular heat-shock/thermotolerance response. This bovine-specific in silico study characterizes all 17 HSP70 genes in the Bos taurus genome, identifies HSPA8 as one of the most highly expressed family members across tissues, and explicitly frames the family as the basis for understanding thermotolerance/adaptive changes in bovines under heat stress. This provides a direct, cattle-specific functional/expression justification for including HSPA8 in a curated panel of heat-stress/thermotolerance candidate genes.
reference: Tripathy K, Sodhi M, Kataria RS, Chopra M, Mukesh M (2020)

basis_for_inclusion: HSPB1 (HSP27) is a small heat-shock protein/molecular chaperone induced as part of the cellular heat-shock response; in cattle its transcription is modulated by heat shock in bovine (Bos taurus) embryos in direct relation to the developmental acquisition of thermotolerance, supporting its inclusion as a candidate for thermotolerance/heat-stress response.
reference: Sakatani M, Bonilla L, Dobbs KB, Block J, Ozawa M, Shanker S, Yao J, Hansen PJ (2013)

basis_for_inclusion: In bovine morula-stage embryos, heat shock (40C/8h) significantly upregulated HSPB11 expression as part of the transcriptomic response associated with developmental acquisition of thermotolerance. This provides direct cattle (Bos taurus) functional/expression evidence linking HSPB11 to heat-stress response and thermotolerance, justifying its inclusion in a curated panel of thermotolerance candidate genes.
reference: Sakatani M, Bonilla L, Dobbs KB, Block J, Ozawa M, Shanker S, Yao J, Hansen PJ (2013)

basis_for_inclusion: HSPB8 (HSP22), a small heat-shock protein chaperone, is directly implicated in the bovine thermal-stress response. Sengar et al. (2017, Cell Stress & Chaperones) profiled miRNAs under summer heat stress in Frieswal (Bos taurus x Bos indicus) crossbred dairy cattle and experimentally validated, via reporter assay in heat-stressed bovine PBMC, that bta-miR-2898 directly targets HSPB8, establishing HSPB8 as a heat-shock-responsive gene regulated during thermal stress in cattle. This justifies its inclusion in a curated panel of bovine thermotolerance candidates (function/expression under heat stress; also listed as a candidate SNP marker gene in cattle thermotolerance reviews, e.g. Hariyono & Prihandini 2022).
reference: Sengar GS, Deb R, Singh U, Raja TV, Kant R, Sajjanar B, Alex R, Alyethodi RR, Kumar A, Kumar S, Singh R, Jakhesara SJ, Joshi CG (2017)

basis_for_inclusion: Direct experimental evidence in cattle: in Girolando (Holstein x Gyr, Bos indicus-cross) dairy cows, heat stress significantly increased expression of the heat-shock protein gene HSPD1 in mammary cells relative to thermoneutral controls (alongside elevated vaginal temperature and cortisol, and reduced milk yield). This functional/expression-under-heat-stress link in Bos taurus/indicus cattle justifies HSPD1's inclusion in a curated panel of thermotolerance/heat-shock candidates. Corroborating support: HSPD1 is also flagged as a candidate thermotolerance biomarker in Caracu beef cattle plasma proteomics (PMID 39538142, DOI 10.1186/s12864-024-11021-7). Source: PubMed.
reference: Mendonca LC, Carvalho WA, Campos MM, Souza GN, de Oliveira SA, Meringhe GKF, Negrao JA (2024)

basis_for_inclusion: In Gyr (Bos indicus) dairy cattle, HSPE1 was identified inside a runs-of-homozygosity (ROH) island shared by >50% of the population, where the authors annotated it specifically as a heat-adaptation gene together with HSF1 and HSPB1 — evidence of selection signatures for environmental/thermal adaptation. This directly supports including HSPE1 in a curated thermotolerance/heat-stress candidate panel in cattle. (Source: PubMed; attribution to be retained.)
reference: Peripolli E, Stafuzza NB, Munari DP, Lima ALF, Irgang R, Machado MA, Panetto JCDC, Ventura RV, Baldi F, da Silva MVGB (2018)

basis_for_inclusion: Genome-wide expression study in cattle (Hariana, Bos indicus; and Vrindavani, B. indicus x B. taurus crossbred) on peripheral blood mononuclear cells under heat stress. HSPH1 was explicitly identified among the heat shock proteins up-regulated (at higher fold change in the crossbred) in response to heat stress, directly supporting its inclusion as a thermotolerance/heat-shock candidate in a curated bovine panel. Source: PubMed.
reference: Sajjanar B, Aalam MT, Khan O, Tanuj GN, Sahoo AP, Manjunathareddy GB, Gandham RK, Dhara SK, Gupta PK, Mishra BP, Dutt T, Singh G (2023)

basis_for_inclusion: IFNT1 (interferon tau) is the maternal-recognition-of-pregnancy signal secreted by the conceptus trophectoderm in cattle: it suppresses endometrial luteolysis and induces interferon-stimulated genes (ISGs) that regulate uterine receptivity, conceptus elongation and implantation.

IGF1 is a candidate gene for cattle reproduction: it regulates ovarian steroidogenesis, granulosa cell function and is associated with reproduction/production traits via SNPs in Holstein (Bos taurus).

Direct bovine heat-stress evidence: Satrapa et al. measured mRNA expression of IGF-system members in in vitro-produced blastocysts of Nellore (Bos indicus) vs Holstein (Bos taurus) under heat stress (41C/9h). IGFBP2 was differentially expressed (higher in heat-stressed Holstein), and its lower expression in Nellore (with high PAPPA) was linked to greater IGF bioavailability and superior heat-stress tolerance. This ties IGFBP2 to thermotolerance and the IGF/growth-reproduction axis in cattle, justifying its inclusion in a curated heat-stress candidate panel.

IL6 (Interleukin-6) is a pro-inflammatory cytokine functionally tied to the bovine heat-stress response. This study experimentally demonstrates that bovine endometrial epithelial (BEND) cells under in vitro heat stress (41 C vs 38.5 C thermoneutral) show increased LPS-induced IL6 expression, linking IL6 to heat-shock protein (HSP1A1/HSF1) regulation and the inflammatory consequences of thermal stress in cattle (reduced fertility, milk production, uterine infection). This direct cattle/Bos taurus functional-expression evidence under heat stress justifies including IL6 in a curated panel of thermotolerance/heat-stress candidate genes. Attribution: data retrieved from PubMed.

An RNA-seq study of bovine granulosa cells (bGCs) exposed to heat stress (39-41 C) identified differentially expressed genes in heat-stress, apoptosis and steroidogenesis pathways, matching the panel trait (reproduction under heat stress, steroidogenesis and granulosa apoptosis in Bos taurus; function/expression under heat stress).
reference: Khan A, Dou J, Wang Y, Jiang X, Khan MZ, Luo H, Usman T, Zhu H (2020)

basis_for_inclusion: MSTN (myostatin/GDF-8) is a negative regulator of skeletal muscle growth; loss-of-function mutations cause the double-muscling phenotype in cattle breeds (e.g. Belgian Blue), driving increased muscle fiber number and mass. This makes MSTN a strong functional candidate for a growth / weight-gain / somatotropic-axis panel in Bos taurus.

PAG1 (pregnancy-associated glycoprotein-1) is secreted by the binucleate trophoblast cells that invade the uterine endometrium during implantation in cattle, and is a central placental marker of uterine receptivity/pregnancy establishment.

The prolactin receptor (PRLR) harbors frameshift "slick" mutations that truncate the receptor and produce a short, sleek hair coat conferring superior body-temperature regulation and thermotolerance in cattle. This review (Hansen 2020, Theriogenology) is a seminal source linking PRLR slick alleles to reduced heat-stress impact on production and reproduction in Bos taurus, justifying PRLR as a curated candidate for a thermotolerance/heat-stress panel.

PTGS2 (COX-2) is a conceptus-regulated prostaglandin-synthesis gene expressed in the bovine endometrium at the initiation of implantation, central to uterine receptivity and maternal recognition of pregnancy.

SCD1 (stearoyl-CoA desaturase) underlies a BTA26 QTL governing milk-fat fatty-acid composition (notably C14 desaturation indices) in dairy cattle, making it a core candidate for milk production / milk-fat traits.

Real cattle heat-stress evidence for SMAD5. According to PubMed, Yang et al. (BMC Genomics, 2025) performed whole-genome bisulfite sequencing of blood from dairy cows comparing spring vs summer, and SMAD5 was one of only three genes (with DNLZ and GNAS) showing the most significant heat-stress-associated change: its promoter DNA methylation was significantly altered and negatively correlated with gene expression under heat stress. This is a direct Bos taurus (dairy cow) heat-stress-response expression/epigenetic association, justifying SMAD5's inclusion in a curated thermotolerance candidate panel. SMAD5 is a BMP/TGF-beta effector, consistent with a regulatory role in the cattle heat-shock response.

A direct heat-stress study in bovine granulosa cells (primary bGCs at 39-41 C) showed reduced viability, estradiol/progesterone (steroidogenesis) and increased apoptosis and ROS; RNA-seq identified DEGs in heat-stress, apoptosis, steroidogenesis and oxidative-stress pathways (including the antioxidant SOD system), covering the panel traits of reproduction under heat stress, steroidogenesis, granulosa apoptosis and oxidative response in Bos taurus.
reference: Khan A, Dou J, Wang Y, Jiang X, Khan MZ, Luo H, Usman T, Zhu H (2020)

basis_for_inclusion: STAR (steroidogenic acute regulatory protein) catalyses the rate-limiting step of steroidogenesis (cholesterol transport to the inner mitochondrial membrane). Li et al. (2016) showed in bovine granulosa cells that heat stress reduces STAR mRNA (with CYP11A1, CYP19A1 and SF-1), decreases estradiol synthesis and induces apoptosis via the BAX/BCL-2 pathway, linking the gene to reproduction under heat stress, steroidogenesis and granulosa apoptosis in cattle.
reference: Li L, Wu J, Luo M, Sun Y, Wang G (2016)

basis_for_inclusion: STAT3 (JAK/STAT3 pathway, activated by LIF/IL-6) regulates cumulus-oocyte complex maturation, cumulus expansion and competence for early embryo development in cattle, supporting its inclusion as a candidate gene for early embryonic development in cattle.

Direct experimental evidence that TNF (TNF-alpha) and its receptors are differentially expressed in dairy cattle (Bos taurus, Holando-Argentino cows) under heat stress: during summer, when animals experienced ~8.5 h/day above THI 68, TNF-alpha and receptor expression dropped sharply versus non-stressful seasons. This links TNF to the bovine heat-stress / immune response, supporting its inclusion as a candidate in a thermotolerance panel. MeSH-indexed for Cattle, Heat Stress Disorders, Heat-Shock Response and Tumor Necrosis Factor-alpha.
Beta-actin; housekeeping/reference locus included as an assay and normalization control (not a phenotype candidate), used to anchor directionality and flag global methylation shifts.
Glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate dehydrogenase; housekeeping/reference locus included as an assay and normalization control (not a phenotype candidate).

HOXA10 is a key marker of endometrial receptivity in cattle: its knockdown activates the FOXO1 pathway, induces apoptosis and alters receptivity genes (ITGB3, ITGAV, MUC1) in bovine endometrial epithelial cells.

HOXA11 is a Mullerian-region homeobox transcription factor essential for endometrial function/receptivity and implantation; in cattle it shows genetic variants (InDels) and phenotype-associated expression profiles, supporting its use as a candidate gene in an endometrial-function/uterine-receptivity panel.
Hypoxanthine phosphoribosyltransferase 1; housekeeping/reference locus included as an assay and normalization control (not a phenotype candidate).

ISG15 is the quintessential interferon-stimulated gene, induced by interferon-tau in the bovine endometrium and PBMCs during maternal recognition of pregnancy, and is a functional biomarker of early pregnancy in cattle.
ITGB3 (integrin beta-3) is an established marker of bovine endometrial receptivity, upregulated by IFN-tau via the IRF1/LIFR axis in the luminal epithelium during the implantation window.
Keratin 18; epithelial marker used as a tissue/quality-control locus (not a phenotype candidate).

LIF (leukemia inhibitory factor) is a master regulator of bovine uterine/endometrial receptivity, driving endometrial epithelial proliferation and the receptivity marker HOXA10 via STAT3 signaling during embryo implantation.

MUC1 (transmembrane mucin glycocalyx) is steroid-regulated in the bovine endometrium and acts as an anti-implantation barrier by steric hindrance; its expression correlates negatively with fertility, supporting it as a candidate gene for uterine receptivity/endometrial function in cattle.
MX1 is a classical antiviral interferon-tau-stimulated gene (ISG) in the bovine endometrium, central to maternal recognition of pregnancy in cattle, connecting antiviral function and fertility.

MX2 is one of the interferon-tau-induced interferon-stimulated genes (ISGs) most upregulated in the bovine endometrium at maternal recognition of pregnancy (Day 16), serving as an antiviral/immune marker of the response to the conceptus.
Ribosomal protein L19; housekeeping/reference locus included as an assay and normalization control (not a phenotype candidate).

RSAD2 (viperin) is one of the interferon-tau-induced interferon-stimulated genes most strongly upregulated in bovine endometrium at maternal recognition of pregnancy, making it a candidate marker of conceptus-driven antiviral/immunomodulatory signaling in cattle.

SPP1 (osteopontin) is an RGD adhesion protein expressed in the bovine endometrium and regulated in the context of tissue remodelling and conceptus-endometrium interaction, and is a functional marker of uterine receptivity/endometrial function in cattle.
Vimentin; mesenchymal marker used as a negative/quality-control locus for epithelial specificity (not a phenotype candidate).
14-3-3 protein zeta/delta (YWHAZ); housekeeping/reference locus included as an assay and normalization control (not a phenotype candidate).

One of the three bovine OAS1 paralogues (X). OAS1 is an interferon-stimulated gene (ISG) strongly induced by conceptus interferon-tau in the bovine endometrium at maternal recognition of pregnancy (Day 16), among the most upregulated genes (>8x log2), making it a candidate marker of uterine receptivity and pregnancy establishment in cattle.

One of the three bovine OAS1 paralogues (Y). OAS1 is an interferon-stimulated gene (ISG) strongly induced by conceptus interferon-tau in the bovine endometrium at maternal recognition of pregnancy (Day 16), among the most upregulated genes (>8x log2), making it a candidate marker of uterine receptivity and pregnancy establishment in cattle.

One of the three bovine OAS1 paralogues (Z). OAS1 is an interferon-stimulated gene (ISG) strongly induced by conceptus interferon-tau in the bovine endometrium at maternal recognition of pregnancy (Day 16), among the most upregulated genes (>8x log2), making it a candidate marker of uterine receptivity and pregnancy establishment in cattle.

ATF4 e o efetor a jusante do eixo UPR/estresse de reticulo endoplasmatico (GRP78->ATF4->CHOP) ativado em celulas bovinas sob estresse termico, ligando a resposta a proteinas mal-enoveladas a apoptose mamaria; candidato funcional plausivel para tolerancia ao calor em bovinos.

ATF6 e um dos tres sensores canonicos da resposta a proteinas mal dobradas (UPR) do reticulo endoplasmatico; em bovinos a clivagem p90ATF6/p50ATF6 atua como chaperona-regulador na adaptacao ao estresse de RE, justificando sua inclusao num painel de genes candidatos para UPR/ER stress sob estresse termico.

DDIT3 (CHOP) is the canonical effector transcription factor of the PERK-ATF4 arm of the unfolded protein response, induced under ER/proteotoxic stress (including heat stress) to commit cells to apoptosis; functional evidence in bovine cells confirms it as a key ER-stress mediator, justifying its inclusion as a UPR/ER-stress candidate gene in cattle.

ERN1 codifica a IRE1, sensor central do estresse de RE e ramo da unfolded protein response (UPR); este estudo mede explicitamente a ativacao (fosforilacao p-IRE1/IRE1) em tecido adiposo bovino sob estresse de RE, justificando ERN1 como gene candidato curado para resposta de UPR/estresse de RE em bovinos.

XBP1 is the IRE1-spliced transcription factor driving the unfolded protein response/ER stress adaptation, demonstrated as functionally active in bovine tissue and thus a candidate for UPR/ER-stress (heat-stress) panels in cattle.

ITGAV (integrin alpha-V) forms alphaV-beta3/beta1/beta5 heterodimers on conceptus trophectoderm that bind osteopontin and other RGD-ligands at the maternal-fetal interface, mediating trophoblast apposition, adhesion and implantation in ruminant/domestic livestock pregnancy.

Integrin beta-1 media a adesao mediada por integrinas do trofectoderma do concepto ao epitelio luminal endometrial durante a cascata de implantacao em bovinos, sustentando fixacao e estabelecimento da gestacao.

Galectina-1 (LGALS1) é expressa em células trofoblásticas gigantes e no estroma/endométrio bovino com perfil espaço-temporal específico durante a gestação, sustentando papel na interface materno-fetal (adesão trofoblástica e implantação) em bovinos.

Galectin-3 (LGALS3) is identified in bovine uterine epithelial cell-derived extracellular vesicles as a progesterone-modulated protein related to implantation and embryo adhesion, supporting a role in trophoblast adhesion and implantation in cattle.
Peptidyl arginine deiminase 4; cis-eQTL and top candidate for R. microplus tick load in Braford cattle (GWAS + skin eQTL).
Central WNT/beta-catenin gene predicted as a candidate mechanism of Braford skin tick resistance.
Cytokine implicated in skin remodelling and immune response of tick-resistant Braford hosts.
Triggering receptor on myeloid cells 1; immune candidate from Gyr × Holstein tick-resistance GWAS network.
Triggering receptor on myeloid cells 2; immune candidate from Gyr × Holstein tick-resistance GWAS network.
Dendritic-cell activation marker; immune candidate from Gyr × Holstein tick-resistance GWAS network.
Myosin VA; immune TF-network candidate from Gyr × Holstein tick-resistance GWAS.
TREM-like 1; immune candidate from Gyr × Holstein tick-resistance GWAS network.
Thymus-specific serine protease; MHC-region immune candidate from Gyr × Holstein tick GWAS.
Interleukin-2; selection-signature immune candidate for tick resistance/immunity in indigenous indicine (Belahi) cattle.
Interleukin-21; selection-signature immune candidate for tick resistance/immunity in indicine cattle.
IL-8 chemokine recruiting granulocytes in the early inflammatory skin response that rejects larvae in resistant hosts.
Monocyte chemoattractant protein-1; pro-inflammatory skin response distinguishing tick-resistant from susceptible hosts.
Alarmin sustaining the pro-inflammatory skin response to tick bite in resistant hosts.
PKR; interferon-inducible kinase sustaining the inflammatory skin response to R. microplus larval attachment.
2'-5'-oligoadenylate synthetase 2; type-I interferon-stimulated gene up-regulated in tick-susceptible bovine skin.
Grainyhead-like 3; skin-barrier transcription factor and DEG in bovine host resistance to ticks.
Deltex-1 (Notch pathway); regulatory DEG in bovine skin host resistance to ticks.
Alpha-S1-casein; major milk-protein locus of the BTA6 casein cluster, associated with milk protein composition in taurine and indicine dairy cattle.
Alpha-S2-casein; BTA6 casein-cluster milk-protein locus with promoter/coding variants affecting milk composition.
Beta-casein; major BTA6 milk-protein locus (A1/A2 variants) affecting milk protein profile and cheese-making traits.
Kappa-casein; BTA6 milk-protein locus affecting milk coagulation and cheese yield.
Beta-lactoglobulin (progestagen-associated endometrial protein); major whey-protein locus (BTA11) associated with milk protein percentage.
Alpha-lactalbumin; regulatory subunit of lactose synthase, key whey protein in milk.
Non-SMC condensin I complex subunit G; growth/milk-production candidate whose SNPs associate with milk protein percentage and yield in Holstein.
Bovine MHC class II (BoLA-DRB3); the BTA23 histocompatibility QTL is a classic determinant of tick resistance in Gyr × Holstein.
